children: London cocoa futures fell sharply on Wednesday, extending the market's retreat from the previous session's one-year high, while arabica coffee prices sank to a five-week low.
COCOA
* London cocoa
slid 5.9% to £4,533 a metric ton by 1332 GMT. The market had risen to a one-year high of £4,988 on Tuesday.
* Dealers said there may still be a global surplus despite an expected decline in production in top grower Ivory Coast in the 2026/27 season that started this week.
* "We expect the global cocoa surplus to narrow sharply from 442,000 tons in 2025/26 to 82,000 tons in 2026/27, underpinning a firmer price floor," BMI analysts said in a note on Wednesday.
* Ample cocoa stockpiles should help to cushion any hit to global production from adverse weather, a Mondelez International executive said on Wednesday.
* New York cocoa
lost 5.9% to $6,181 a ton.
COFFEE
* Arabica coffee
was down 2.1% at $3.03 per lb after hitting a five-week low of $2.9905.
* Dealers said there had been a pick-up in exports from Brazil as the harvest nears its end, helping to ease short-term supply tightness.

* Cooxupe, Brazil's largest coffee cooperative, said on Wednesday that its farmers had harvested 91.9% of their 2026 crop by August 28, up from 87.5% a week earlier but lagging the 94.9% at the same point last year.
* Robusta coffee
lost 1% to $3,426 a ton after matching a 2-1/2-month low of $3,405 set on Tuesday.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
rose 0.3% to 18.41 cents per lb after climbing by 3.1% on Tuesday.

* Dealers said tight supplies and strong domestic prices in top consumer India helped to fuel the recent run-up in prices, along with the prospect of lower production in the European Union and Thailand.
* White sugar
lost 0.1% to $533.40 a ton.
